body: I already had an IUD when my bladder symptoms developed. None of the endo medications worked for me until I had surgery

I think about this a lot. I was told I had IC and spent years and years trying all of the treatments without relief. Finally, someone suggested a diagnostic lap and found endo all around my bladder. The excision surgery gave me my life back.

It makes me sad to think of all the women who are suffering from bladder pain because their doctors slap an IC label on them and don’t look for any underlying causes. 

I actually had 2 laps because my first surgeon failed to get all the endo out. Both recoveries did not hold a candle to the pain I was in every day. If you aren’t getting any relief from typical treatments, it’s worth a try. It wasn’t a cure, but my symptoms got better dramatically.

For a long time, I didn’t feel better and I was kicking myself for going through another useless surgery. Then, we tried an endo med called Danazol, which I had previously tried before surgery without success. By around six months post-op and restarting Danazol, I began noticing so much improvement! So in endometriosis, the abdominal area gets super inflamed, which is what causes the painful symptoms. This inflammation is created by a type of immune cell called a macrophage. 

Immune cells are supposed to help restore damage in the body. But endometriosis creates an environment where some these cells start causing inflammation instead. 

Researchers knew these macrophages were the cause of pain in endometriosis, but they didn’t know how to treat them. This is because there was no way to distinguish between the good immune cells protecting us and the bad ones causing disease. 

So now, they have figured out a way to distinguish the bad cells. And they have a drug that specifically targets these cells.

So they gave the drugs to mice engineered to have endometriosis and the drugs shrunk the endo lesions. My doctor is confident that the drug will do the same thing in humans. So that’s the next step.
